page: Microsoft Azure M64bds_1_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C x86_64 processor operating at 4.0 GHz, offering 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with dedicated hyperthreading. Cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 105 MB L3 cache pool. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography extensions such as AES and SHA-NI.

Hardware allocations feature 1397.0 GB of memory, equating to 21.83 GB per vCPU, and a bundled 3221 GB local SSD for high-speed scratch storage. No dedicated GPUs are included, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory and computing performance. Memory throughput reaches 4519.69 GB/sec for small cached reads and 216.95 GB/sec for uncached large reads. In compute and database workloads, the system delivers strong performance, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 66425.61, a Geekbench multi-core score of 19691.0, and 70.71 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Image processing benchmarks register in the top 10 percent tier.

The CPU includes AMX capabilities, yielding strong LLM prompt processing speeds across model sizes. However, text generation on a 70B parameter model reaches only 2.58 tokens per second due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware. Given its high memory density and strong sequential bandwidth, the instance represents a cost-effective alternative to multi-instance clustering for large in-memory databases like SAP HANA or Redis, large-scale ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency transactional database engines.
description: Microsoft Azure M64bds_1_v3 is a memory-optimized cloud server delivering 64 vCPUs and 1397.0 GB of RAM, backed by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at 4.0 GHz. Designed with a massive memory allocation of 21.83 GB per vCPU and 3221 GB of integrated local SSD storage, it is tailored for enterprise memory footprints. Compute evaluation displays strong results, including a PassMark CPU score of 66425.61, 70.71 million Redis SET operations per second, and 216.95 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. Hardware AMX instructions provide strong token processing for smaller LLM models, though large-model generation throughput remains limited without dedicated GPUs. This instance delivers resource-dense scalability for large in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, and intensive relational database workloads.
